Native sparse future split-conformal workflow with optional Python W2 scientific record

etr_run_sparse_prediction_workflow.Rd

Split-conformal coverage applies only to future observed measurements on the explicitly declared finite grid, not continuous-time latent trajectories. The process performs no random role allocation or raw interpolation. Python runtime classes, full error semantics and independent certification remain outside the R source-scientific record.

Usage

etr_run_sparse_prediction_workflow(proper_training, calibration,
    target, config, strict_source_record = FALSE)

Arguments

proper_training

An explicit native irregular proper-training trajectory set.

calibration

A separate native irregular calibration trajectory set.

target

Exactly one native irregular target trajectory.

config

Named sparse prediction configuration with explicit training, history_cutoff, and finite prediction_grid. The backend="native_sparse_partial_conformal" computes source-scientific PACE conditional predictions and calibration bands; native_mean_curve_split_conformal is a distinct alternative.

strict_source_record

If TRUE, require native sparse PACE training, preserve its nested frozen W2 scientific record, and emit the eleven canonical source result fields, nine configuration fields, scientific decisions and explicit disjoint-role provenance. Reject R-only selector fold replay. Default FALSE retains native extended diagnostic results.

Value

A native scientific workflow recording training FPCA/PACE, calibration, a single target prediction band, measured steps, scientific decisions, reports and tables.
